translationRepairs: He had eleven sons: Yuqing, Chongqing, and Chongqing; the names of the rest are lost.
He had eleven sons: Yuqing, Chongqing, and another Chongqing; the names of the other eight are lost.

s0087 names three distinct sons 餘慶、重慶、崇慶; the latter two are homonymous in pinyin. 'Another Chongqing' preserves that they are distinct people, while 'the other eight' correctly recovers 十一子 minus the three named.
Eleven sons: Yuqing, Chongqing, Chongqing—the names of the rest are lost.
Eleven sons: Yuqing, Chongqing, and another Chongqing; the names of the other eight are lost.
The literal field has the same two homonymous names. 'Another Chongqing' distinguishes the two people without Chinese parentheticals, and 'the other eight' matches the count.
On Mount Ming a tiger was ravaging the countryside. Tianzhang petitioned the spirit of Mount Wenshan, and it was immediately captured.
On Mount Ming a tiger was ravaging the countryside. Tianzhang sent a formal communication to the mountain spirit, and the tiger was immediately captured.
移文山神 is a formal dispatch to the mountain spirit, not a petition to a place "Mount Wenshan" (misparsing 文山); 立捕獲之 refers to the tiger, which the replacement makes explicit.
On Mount Ming a tiger was ravaging; Tianzhang petitioned the spirit of Mount Wenshan and immediately captured it.
On Mount Ming a tiger was ravaging; Tianzhang sent a formal communication to the mountain spirit, and the tiger was immediately captured.
Same misparse of 移文山神 as "spirit of Mount Wenshan"; the proposed literal correctly treats 移文 as sending an official communication and keeps the tiger as the captured object.

He also halted the practice of the surveillance office's fine-forfeiture funds not being remitted to headquarters, keeping them for famine relief. When censors arrived, the people blocked the road to praise him.

He also ordered that the surveillance office's fine-forfeiture funds not be remitted to headquarters, retaining them for famine relief. When censors arrived, the people blocked the road to praise him.
止…不輸於台，留用賑饑 means he stopped remitting the fine-forfeiture funds to headquarters and kept them for famine relief; "halted the practice of … not being remitted" reverses that sense.

He also halted the practice of the surveillance office's fine-forfeiture funds not being remitted to headquarters, keeping them for famine relief; when censors arrived, the people blocked the road to praise him.

He also stopped the surveillance office's fine-forfeiture funds from being remitted to headquarters and retained them for famine relief; when censors arrived, the people blocked the road to praise him.
The literal has the same reversed double negative; stopping remittance to 台 and retaining the funds for famine relief matches 止…不輸於台，留用賑饑.
